sourcedFrom: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 (2024)
cleanIntro: The Crossfire is a FireStick rifle, and that changes what cleaning even means. The propellant arrives in a sealed Federal Firestick capsule, so there is NO removable breech plug to pull and no blow-back fouling the action from behind. Two things are specific to this rifle and appear nowhere in a conventional inline's routine: an internal Bullet Seating Ring in the bore that CVA forbids you to remove and that will stop your jag short of the breech, and a firing pin assembly that is serviced only when something has gone wrong.

steps.title: Check the serial number against CVA's recall
steps.action: Read the serial number off the barrel — it is underneath, beneath the forearm — and check how it ends. CVA recalled a range of older in-line guns by serial number, and only the number on your own gun can settle whether yours is one of them.
steps.prose: No listing or guide can resolve this for you; it is a fact about your individual firearm. If the number ends in -95 or -96, stop and call CVA before doing anything else.
steps.quote: Example of a recalled serial number: 61-13-XXXXXX-95 If you, or someone you know, have a CVA in-line with such a serial number, do not use or allow anyone else to use the gun under any circumstances.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Voluntary Recall, p.17
steps.warn: A recalled serial number means the gun is not to be used by anyone, including anyone you lend it to.

steps.title: Break the action open and look through the barrel
steps.action: Pull the breeching lever — it is built into the trigger guard — rearward until the action unlocks, then pivot the barrel forward to open the breech. Now look through the bore from the breech end. You are looking for light.
steps.prose: Light through the barrel is the proof. Anything less than a clear view means you treat the gun as loaded and clear it before going on.
steps.caution: If you cannot see light through the barrel, assume it is loaded and push the obstruction out with a range rod longer than the under-barrel rod.
steps.quote: Pull the breeching lever rearward until the action unlocks. Pivot the barrel forward to open the breech. Verify the gun is unloaded by looking through the barrel. If you cannot see light through the barrel, you must assume it is loaded.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Getting Started, p.7

steps.title: Remove the primer and the Firestick
steps.action: With the breech open, take the 209 shotshell primer out of the rear of the Firestick capsule, then lift the Firestick itself out of the breech.
steps.prose: Two separate items in a fixed order — primer first, then the charge. The Firestick is the entire powder charge in one sealed capsule, which is why removing it empties the chamber outright rather than leaving loose powder behind.
steps.quote: 1. Open the breech of the rifle. 2. Remove the 209 Shotshell Primer from the Firestick™ propellant capsule. 3. Remove the Firestick™ propellant capsule from the breech of the rifle.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Unloading Your CVA Crossfire Muzzleloader, p.11

steps.title: Push the bullet out breech-to-muzzle
steps.action: The bullet is still seated in the bore. Take the jag OFF a range rod longer than the barrel so the rod will pass through the Bullet Seating Ring, then push the bullet from the breech end out through the muzzle.
steps.prose: The direction is the opposite of what a conventional muzzleloader teaches. The bullet is seated against a ring partway up the bore, and the only clear path is forward and out the front.
steps.caution: A rod with a jag on it will not pass the Bullet Seating Ring. Some rods are too fat in the shank to pass it at all — check before you start pushing.
steps.quote: Using a range rod (longer than the length of the barrel) with the jag removed (to allow passage through the Bullet Seating Ring), push the bullet out of the barrel from breech to muzzle.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Unloading Your CVA Crossfire Muzzleloader, p.11

steps.title: Never remove the Bullet Seating Ring
steps.action: Leave the Bullet Seating Ring alone. It is a factory-installed part inside the bore, and it is not a cleaning obstruction to be got rid of — it is what stops the bullet at the correct depth.
steps.prose: It will feel like it is in your way, because it stops the jag short of the breech every time you clean. That is the design working, not a fault.
steps.quote: Do not make any attempt at removing this important part from your barrel. Removal, or attempts at removing the ring will void your warranty and compromise the function and safe loading of your rifle.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Loading Your CVA Crossfire, p.10
steps.warn: Removing it, or trying to, voids the warranty and compromises safe loading.

steps.title: Take the forestock screw out and open the action
steps.action: Confirm the gun is unloaded once more. Then, with a properly fitting screwdriver, remove the single screw from the centre of the fore stock, pull the breeching lever to the rear and open the action.
steps.prose: A properly fitting screwdriver means one that fills the slot — a narrow blade will round the head of a screw you have to take out after every shooting session.
steps.quote: 1. Verify gun is unloaded. 2. Using a properly fitting screwdriver, remove the screw from the center of the fore stock. 3. Pull the breeching lever to the rear and open the action.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Cleaning Procedure, p.13

steps.title: Push the bulk of the fouling out from the muzzle
steps.action: Put a jag on a cleaning rod, wet a patch with solvent and push it through from the MUZZLE end. Run one or two through to carry off the loose fouling.
steps.prose: The jag will stop dead when it reaches the Bullet Seating Ring near the breech — that is expected, and it is as far as a jag goes from this direction. The short section of Firestick chamber beyond the ring is reached from the breech end instead.
steps.quote: Using a jag on a cleaning rod, push a solvent soaked patch or two through the barrel from the muzzle end to remove the bulk of the fouling from the bore. Note that the jag will stop when it hits the Bullet Seating Ring near the breech of the rifle.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Cleaning Procedure, step 4, p.13

steps.title: Brush the bore wet
steps.action: Swap the jag for a properly fitting bore brush, wet it with solvent and make several full-length strokes through the barrel.
steps.prose: Full-length strokes, and the brush stays wet — a dry brush polishes fouling rather than lifting it.
steps.quote: Place a properly fitting bore brush on the rod and make several fulllength strokes through the barrel. The brush should be wet with solvent for this step.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Cleaning Procedure, step 5, p.13

steps.title: Patch wet, let it work, then patch dry
steps.action: Take the brush off and go back to the jag. Push several damp solvent patches through, give the solvent a minute or two to work, then follow with dry clean patches. Repeat until the barrel is clean, and finish with a non-petroleum gun oil to protect the bore.
steps.prose: The pause is the part people skip. Black powder fouling is hygroscopic salt as much as it is carbon, and the solvent needs a moment on it before the dry patch comes through.
steps.quote: Remove the brush from the rod and use the jag to push several patches damp with solvent through the bore. Allow the solvent to work for a minute or two and follow with dry, clean patches. Repeat until the barrel is clean.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Cleaning Procedure, step 6, p.13

steps.title: Scrub the breech face and the action areas
steps.action: Use a solvent-wet patch on the breech face and whatever else of the action you can reach; cotton swabs get into the corners. Wipe everything dry with a clean patch or rag and put rust preventative on it.
steps.prose: This is where the primer residue actually lands on a Crossfire — the sealed Firestick keeps combustion products out of the bore-side breech, but the primer still fires into the breech face.
steps.quote: Use a patch wet with solvent to scrub the breech face and other action areas that you can reach. Cotton swabs can be used to reach smaller areas. Wipe dry with a clean patch or rag and apply rust preventative.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Cleaning Procedure, step 7, p.13

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Forestock screw back in, action closed, bore clean and oiled, breech face wiped and protected. Reassemble the gun, check every mechanical function, and wipe the whole outside with rust preventative.
steps.prose: There is no breech plug step on this rifle and no bolt to open — the Firestick capsule seals the chamber, so the routine ends here. If the barrel is nitride treated you have longer before cleaning becomes urgent, but the untreated parts still need it on the normal schedule.
steps.quote: Reassemble the gun and check all mechanical functions. Wipe the entire gun with a rust preventative.
steps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Cleaning Procedure, step 8, p.13

deepSteps.title: Know when the firing pin actually needs service
deepSteps.action: Do not put the firing pin assembly on a routine schedule. Service it when a Firestick has ruptured, or when the gun has been soaked — and otherwise leave it alone.
deepSteps.prose: On a conventional inline the breech plug blows combustion gas back onto the firing pin every shot, so it fouls constantly. The Crossfire's sealed capsule removes that path entirely, which is why CVA scopes this job to specific events rather than a round count.
deepSteps.quote: Unlike conventional in-line muzzleloaders, the Crossfire chamber is sealed by the Firestick™ encapsulated powder charge. There is no blow-back from the breechplug to foul the firing pin assembly.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Maintaining the Firing Pin Assembly, p.13

deepSteps.title: Remove and clean the firing pin and spring
deepSteps.action: Verify the gun is unloaded. Cock the hammer so the rear of the firing pin is exposed, then remove the screw above the firing pin — the pin and its spring will follow it out. Clean and lubricate the pin, the spring and the firing pin hole in the frame, then reassemble in reverse order.
deepSteps.prose: The retaining screw sits directly above the pin, and cocking the hammer is what gives you access to it. Pin and spring come out together as the screw clears.
deepSteps.caution: The spring is captive behind that screw. Take the screw out over a bench, not over the floor.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Verify the gun is unloaded 2. Cock the hammer to expose the rear of the firing pin 3. Remove the screw above the firing pin 4. The firing pin and spring will follow. 5. Clean and lubricate the pin, spring, and the firing pin hole in the frame. 6. Reassemble in reverse order.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Maintaining the Firing Pin Assembly, p.14

deepSteps.title: Prove the pin protrudes and retracts
deepSteps.action: With the gun unloaded and the action open so you can see the firing pin hole in the breech face, hold the trigger back so the hammer can be pushed forward into the frame. Watch the pin come through the hole, then watch it withdraw as the hammer is released.
deepSteps.prose: Both halves matter. A pin that protrudes but does not retract is a slam-fire waiting to happen when the next Firestick is seated.
deepSteps.quote: b. Open the rife to expose the firing pin hole in the breech face. c. Hold the trigger to the rear so that the hammer can be pushed forward into the frame. d. Look to be certain the firing pin protrudes from the firing pin hole and properly retracts into the hole as the hammer is released.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Maintaining the Firing Pin Assembly, step 7, p.14
deepSteps.warn: If the firing pin does not retract properly, stop. This is a call to CVA for professional servicing, not something to file, bend or spring-swap at home.

deepSteps.title: Stop if the pin fails its check
deepSteps.action: A firing pin that will not retract when the hammer is released ends the job. Contact CVA Customer Service about servicing it.
deepSteps.prose: CVA also notes that some internal frame parts have to be fitted by their gunsmith and are only sold as installed parts — this is one of the places that applies.
deepSteps.quote: e. If the firing pin fails to retract properly when the hammer is released, contact CVA Customer Service regarding professional servicing of the firing pin.
deepSteps.cite: CVA Crossfire Owner's Manual — No. CF_MAN Rev. 07/24 — Maintaining the Firing Pin Assembly, step 7e, p.14

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Solvent patch or two from the MUZZLE end to carry off loose fouling
Expect the jag to stop at the Bullet Seating Ring — clean the Firestick chamber from the breech end instead
Wet bore brush, several full-length strokes
Damp solvent patches, wait a minute or two, then dry patches; repeat until clean
Finish with a non-petroleum gun oil to protect the bore

cleaning.name: Breech and action
tasks: Solvent-wet patch on the breech face and reachable action areas
Wipe dry, then apply rust preventative

cleaning.name: Exterior
tasks: Reassemble and check all mechanical functions
Wipe the entire gun with rust preventative

reassembly: Close the action and refit the fore stock screw with a properly fitting screwdriver.
If the firing pin was removed, reassemble in reverse order and refit the retaining screw above the pin.
Check every mechanical function: breech opening and closing, hammer cocking and releasing, and the firing pin protruding and retracting.
Wipe the entire gun with rust preventative.
fncheck: With the gun unloaded and the breech open, hold the trigger to the rear and push the hammer forward: the firing pin must protrude from the firing pin hole in the breech face and must retract back into the hole when the hammer is released. If it does not retract, contact CVA Customer Service.
